title: Satlyt, founded by a former Google and SpaceX product manager, raises $8M to run AI on satellites
summary: Satlyt, a startup founded by former Google and SpaceX executives, secured $8M in funding to enable AI computing on satellites through open-source software. The company positions itself as an alternative to SpaceX's proprietary approach, offering interoperable solutions across multiple satellite platforms.
content: Satlyt wants to be the Android of orbital computing, offering open software that works on many companies' satellites, versus SpaceX's closed, all-in-one iPhone-style approach.

zh.title: 由前谷歌和SpaceX产品经理创办的Satlyt融资800万美元在卫星上运行AI
zh.summary: 由前谷歌和SpaceX高管创办的初创公司Satlyt获得800万美元融资，通过开源软件在卫星上实现AI计算。该公司将自己定位为SpaceX专有方案的替代品，为多个卫星平台提供互操作解决方案。

title: Huawei made a whole camera to attach to its latest phone
summary: Huawei's Ruiying Z10 camera attachment for its Mate 90 Pro Max flagship features a 1-inch, 50-megapixel RYYB sensor larger than any inside the phone itself, providing major upgrades in zoom and photography capabilities. This represents a significant leap beyond typical teleconverter lens attachments common among Chinese Android manufacturers.
content:
I’m sorry, this is just a camera that makes phone calls. | Image: Huawei	

Over the last few years, Chinese Android manufacturers have followed Vivo's example of launching add-on "teleconverter" lenses for their flagship phones, enabling long-distance photography that the phones on their own could never match. Today, Huawei one-upped everybody with the add-on lens for its Mate 90 Pro Max flagship, which is not only a comically huge zoom lens, but also includes its own image sensor.

title: This very fancy e-bike is one of the first to go semi-solid state
summary: The Lemmo 3 cargo bike is among the first e-bikes to feature a semi-solid state battery, offering improved safety and energy density compared to traditional lithium-ion batteries. This technology reduces thermal runaway risk and enables compact charging while improving range and longevity.
content:
Lemmo wants you to call it an SUV. | Image: Lemmo	

The Lemmo 3 is the first cargo bike from the respected German e-bike maker. This premium, step-through longtail is a slightly less insane take on Rivian's Also TM-B, with one major advantage: It's one of the first electric bikes to feature a semi-solid state battery. 
Semi-solid state batteries are far safer than traditional lithium-ion batteries. Their gel-like composition offers improved energy density, with far less risk of thermal runaway. That translates to improved range and longevity from a more compact battery that's unlikely to catch fire when left charging overnight in your house or business. title: The People of Utah vs. Kevin O’Leary
summary: Venture capitalist Kevin O'Leary's 40,000-acre Wonder Valley data center project in Utah faces significant local resistance despite county commissioner approval and plans for a 9 gigawatt gas power plant. O'Leary has attributed the opposition to Chinese interference, a claim disputed by local residents and critics.
content:
On the morning of May 11th, the celebrity investor Kevin O’Leary appeared on Fox Business and announced that he was under attack by Chinese agents. 
For weeks, he had been going on TV and posting online to tout his project, called Wonder Valley, after his nickname from the reality show Shark Tank, Mr. Wonderful. It was going to be enormous, “the largest data center in the world,” sitting on 40,000 acres north of Great Salt Lake in rural Box Elder County, Utah. A dedicated gas power plant would tap into an interstate pipeline and generate 9 gigawatts of electricity, more than double the average consumption of the entire state. The project was coming so fast, thanks to Utah’s governor and legislative leaders, O’Leary said, that “it shows China and the rest of the world we aren’t messing around.”
But now, wearing a black baseball cap printed with the words “Utah National Security,” he told Maria Bartiromo that he had noticed something baffling. Ever since the three county commissioners unanimously approved his data center the week before, O’Leary had observed a sudden increase in people mad at him online. For this he could see only one explanation. 
“Who would want us to stop building our electrical grid? Who would want to stop us from having compute capacity to develop AI? Which adversary would want that?” he asked Bartiromo. “There’s only one: It’s China.”
“I got my guys to go a deep dig into the IP addresses,” he told Bartiromo. Brandishing a sheet of paper, he began to read the names of people who had — or he believed to be somehow connected to people who had — criticized his data center online. 
“Come out, come out, wherever you are and let’s shine the light of transparency on what you’re doing,” he exclaimed, looking up from his paper to address the camera and inviting them to clear their names. “It’s the CPP [sic] at work here. There’s no question about it.”

title: Noise from Universal’s latest ride made rich locals furious, fast
summary: Universal Studios Hollywood agreed to install additional sound barriers around its Fast & Furious: Hollywood Drift ride following complaints from nearby residents about noise from the 72 mph attraction. The park also committed to limiting early morning operations through year-end to mitigate impact.
content:
Don’t have too much fun, you’ll upset the neighbors. | Photo: Ronaldo Bolaños / Los Angeles Times via Getty Images	

Universal Studios Hollywood has pledged to erect another sound barrier around its latest attraction after local residents complained about the bloodcurdling screams from riders. In a meeting attended by at least 350 people yesterday, park execs also promised that Fast & Furious: Hollywood Drift won't operate between 8AM and 9AM for the rest of the year, Deadline reports.

title: Vivo’s X Fold 6 accidentally feels like a throwback
summary: The Vivo X Fold 6 launched in China in June but feels outdated by its global release as Apple and Samsung have since shifted to shorter, wider foldable designs. Its 6.51-inch standard aspect ratio cover display and visible crease place it behind current competitors.
content:
The X Fold 6 looks like foldables did three months ago.	

It's a quirk of the release calendar that when Vivo's X Fold 6 launched in China this June, it was just another foldable. Now that it's ready for its global release, the size and aspect ratio feel oddly old-fashioned.
The X Fold 6 is much the same size as Vivo's previous foldables, and most other foldables that launched before both Apple and Samsung pivoted to a shorter, wider form factor with the Z Fold 8 and iPhone Duo. The 6.51-inch cover display is in the standard smartphone 20:9 aspect ratio, opening to an almost square 8.02-inch panel. The crease is a little behind rivals, since it's quite visible, and the IP59 rating is good but not  …

zh.title: Vivo X Fold 6 无意间显得过时

title: Elon Musk’s Grokipedia has a ‘newly refreshed’ design
summary: Grokipedia, SpaceX AI's Wikipedia competitor, received a v0.3 redesign featuring a new logo, featured articles list, most-read tracker, and live edits page, expanding beyond its minimal previous interface.
content:
Grokipedia, SpaceXAI's AI-powered competitor to Wikipedia, recently started incorporating edits again, and today, it got some design tweaks as part of a v0.3 update, including a new logo and refreshes to its homepage and live edits page. SpaceXAI head of design Benji Taylor calls it a "newly refreshed Grokipedia."
Grokipedia's old homepage was pretty much just a logo and a search bar, but the updated homepage includes a list of featured articles, a list of the most-read articles, and a tracker showing the "latest edits."
